blocks.text: In verses 38–41, Matthew presents Jonah’s “three days and three nights” in the fish as a comparison with the Son of Man’s time “in the heart of the earth,” while also pointing to Nineveh’s response to Jonah’s preaching. This is narrated and typological language; attempts to calculate an exact chronology from the phrase, or to make the details of Jonah’s fish experience carry the main weight of the passage, go beyond what these verses establish. Matthew’s formulation differs from Luke’s, which foregrounds Jonah himself and his proclamation as the sign. These comparisons are debated, so the text’s stated connections should be distinguished from more precise reconstructions.
